description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol is privileged and singleton: only the DDE application
manager may bind it, and at most one client may bind it at a time
within a given user session. It lets that client obtain an
xdg-activation-v1 token for an application it is about to launch.
The compositor only checks the caller's identity; deciding whether
an application may be activated is the client's responsibility.

A token obtained through this protocol is accepted by
xdg_activation_v1.activate() from any client. Even though it
carries no serial and no originating surface, a still-valid token
is never downgraded to an attention request for that reason. Each
token is one-shot and expires after a limited time; see the
treeland_activation_token_v1 interface for the detailed semantics.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document
are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A privileged, singleton global that mints xdg-activation-v1
tokens for the DDE application manager.

Only the DDE application manager may bind this interface, and
only one client may bind it at a time within a given user
session. The compositor must reject bind attempts from
non-privileged clients by sending a protocol error
(not_privileged), and must reject a second concurrent bind
attempt by sending a protocol error (binding_rejected).

Destroy the treeland_activation_token_manager_v1 object and
release the singleton binding. The compositor accepts a new
binding from another client after this request is processed.
Tokens already delivered through this manager are not
affected.

Create a treeland_activation_token_v1 object. The compositor
mints the token and delivers it with the token event on the
new object.

Each request_token call mints an independent token.
Multiple outstanding (unconsumed and unexpired) tokens may
coexist; requesting a new token does not consume,
invalidate, or expire any previously issued token.

description.text:
A token object delivers exactly one token event and is then
inert. The token is one-shot: only the first
xdg_activation_v1.activate() request that uses it produces a
real activation and consumes the token. The token also expires
after a limited time. Once consumed or expired, a subsequent
activate() with the same token produces no activation and is
downgraded to an attention request instead.

The client should destroy the object after receiving the token,
to release the object and its associated compositor resources.

Destroy the treeland_activation_token_v1 object. This does
not invalidate a token that was already delivered.

Sent once, in response to the request_token request that
created this object. The event is delivered as part of that
request's dispatch, so the client must add its listener
before the next wl_display_dispatch()/roundtrip().
